ut_globe_the.blurb: The Globe is a single house-sized sandstone boulder just inside the south entrance of Zion National Park, west of the gate, with about ten lines in all. Nearly all are boulder problems, from VB up through V2, with one V5 and a single harder sport-graded traverse around the whole block. The rock is tall, so more than one crash pad is a sensible thing to bring, and the down-climb is on the southwest corner. The boulder has a few bolts on top, so some faces can also be top-roped. Flooding in 2021 piled sediment around the base, which has changed how the problems start. Sandstone here is fragile when wet, so wait for dry conditions.

ut_golden_boulders_the.blurb: The Golden Boulders is a small bouldering zone in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Central Wasatch, at roughly 5,800 feet. It holds about ten problems and nothing else, spread from V1 up to V10, with most of the weight in the V4 to V8 range, so it suits climbers working at an intermediate to hard level more than beginners. Maples overhead give dappled light, and the boulders sit a short way back from the road, which tends to keep the numbers down. The area is known for a few standout problems at the top end alongside several moderates.

ut_lobster_rock.blurb: Lobster Rock is a quartzite boulder in the Lower Boulder Field above Ogden, in the northern Wasatch. It offers about ten problems, all bouldering, graded V1 to V3 with an even split between the easiest and hardest grades, which makes it a friendly stop for newer boulderers. Expect some dynamic moves, mostly decent landings, and top-outs that get slick when the stone is warm. The lines face west and south, and a trail leads straight to it from 24th Street or Lake Drive, so the walk is short. The wider field can be climbed year round.

ut_s_curve_boulders.blurb: This is a compact bouldering spot in Big Cottonwood Canyon, close to the highway just above the S-curve, at around 6,200 feet. It has roughly ten problems and they are hard: they start around V5 and climb through V7 to V12, so it is a place for experienced boulderers rather than a warm-up venue. The rock can feel loose in places, which adds risk, and a few pads are worth bringing. The boulders sit a short scramble down a small talus slope from the road, so the walk-in is brief.

ut_utahnics_wall.blurb: Utahnics Wall is a quartzite wall of about 50 feet on the lower tier near the south end of the Schoolroom cliff band above Ogden. It has about ten routes mixing trad, sport and top-rope: grades run from 5.6 to the low 5.12s, with most in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, so it works well for climbers wanting easier mileage. An overhanging arete and a right-facing dihedral mark the far left side. The rock is not the finest, but the lines are worthwhile. You scramble up talus to reach the base, and the wall also gives a way up to the second tier.

ut_basement_the.blurb: The Basement is a ledge-based sector in the northern Schoolroom above Ogden, on a lower tier beneath the main Asbury Park wall. It has about ten routes, mostly sport with a few trad lines, and it is a steep-end venue: one route near 5.9, then mostly 5.11 through 5.13. Quartzite is the rock type of the cliff band. To get onto the ledge you can rappel in or scramble down a slab at the north edge of Asbury Park. It is not a place for beginners, and the hard grades mean many lines see few ascents.
